what_its_for: Tirzepatide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes (Mounjaro). It is also used to help with weight loss in adults who are overweight or obese (Zepbound). It works by acting like two natural hormones in your body that help control blood sugar, slow down digestion, and reduce hunger so you eat less.
how_to_take: Tirzepatide comes as a liquid in a pre-filled injection pen. You inject it under your skin (subcutaneous injection) once a week on the same day each week. You can give the injection in your belly (abdomen), thigh, or upper arm. Rotate the injection site each week so you do not use the exact same spot. You can take it with or without food. If you need to change your weekly injection day, make sure your doses are at least 3 days apart.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over time to reduce side effects. The usual starting dose is 2.5 mg once a week for 4 weeks. After that, your doctor may increase your dose every 4 weeks as needed. The dose can go up to 5 mg, 7.5 mg, 10 mg, 12.5 mg, or a maximum of 15 mg once weekly. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and your next scheduled dose is more than 4 days away, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If your next scheduled dose is in 3 days or less, skip the missed dose and take your next dose on your regular scheduled day. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store unused pens in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep them in the original carton to protect them from light. Do not freeze tirzepatide and do not use it if it has been frozen. If needed, you can store the pen at room temperature (up to 86°F or 30°C) for up to 21 days. Once a pen has been used, throw it away safely in a puncture-resistant sharps container. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can affect your blood sugar. Do not share your injection pen with anyone else, even if the needle has been changed. Avoid getting pregnant while taking tirzepatide, as it may harm an unborn baby. Stop taking it at least 2 months before planning to get pregnant and talk to your doctor about other options. Avoid driving or operating machinery if you feel dizzy or lightheaded, especially when starting the medication.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: severe stomach pain that does not go away and may spread to your back (this could be a sign of pancreatitis); signs of a serious allergic reaction such as swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, severe rash, or trouble breathing; vision changes or problems with your eyes; signs of low blood sugar such as shaking, sweating, fast heartbeat, dizziness, or confusion (especially if you take other diabetes medications); signs of kidney problems such as urinating less than normal or swelling in your legs or feet; a lump or swelling in your neck, trouble swallowing, or hoarseness (possible signs of a thyroid tumor); or yellowing of the skin or eyes (possible sign of gallbladder problems). Also call your doctor if nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea is severe or does not improve.
when_it_works: You may notice a reduction in your appetite within the first few weeks of starting tirzepatide. Blood sugar improvements may begin within the first 1 to 2 weeks. For weight loss, most people start to see meaningful results within 4 to 12 weeks, with greater results seen over several months. The full benefit is usually seen after being on a stable dose for several months. This medication works best when combined with a healthy diet and regular physical activity.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use tirzepatide if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Stop taking it at least 2 months before trying to get pregnant and talk to your doctor about safe alternatives. Kidney or liver problems: Use with caution. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Older adults (65 and older): Tirzepatide can be used, but older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like nausea and dehydration. Make sure to drink enough fluids. Children: Tirzepatide is not approved for use in people under 18 years of age. Type 1 diabetes: This medication is not approved for type 1 diabetes. Personal or family history of thyroid cancer (medullary thyroid carcinoma) or a condition called MEN 2: Do not use tirzepatide. Tell your doctor about your full medical history before starting this medication.
